props.name: open
props.description: The open state. By default it goes in the two directions: use `bind:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The open state at the start, for when you give no `open`.

props.name: controlledOpen
props.description:
Give your own code full control of the open state. The component stops to write back to
`open`, and it reports only through `onOpenChange`. Thus the parent can refuse a change: the
parent does not send the new value down. The default is off, because `bind:open` is the usual
case and it needs the write-back.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the open state changes.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge of the panel.

props.name: modal
props.description: How the drawer holds the focus and stops the page scroll. Read `DrawerModal`.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Lets a swipe toward the anchored edge dismiss the drawer.

props.name: shouldCloseOnEscape
props.description: Closes the drawer when the user pushes the `Escape` key.

props.name: shouldCloseOnInteractOutside
props.description: Closes the panel when the user presses outside it.

props.name: snapPoints
props.description:
The rest positions of the panel. They can be in any sequence, because the component sorts
them. `DrawerSnapPoint` gives the value forms that the prop accepts. Without this prop, the
drawer is open or closed, and nothing between.

props.name: snapPoint
props.description: The current snap point. By default it goes in the two directions: use `bind:snapPoint`.

props.name: defaultSnapPoint
props.description: The snap point at the start, for when you give no `snapPoint`.

props.name: onSnapPointChange
props.description: The component calls it when the current snap point changes.

props.name: snapToSequentialPoints
props.description:
Stops a fast flick at the next snap point. Use it when each step has a meaning, and a jump of
two steps would confuse the user.

props.name: handle
props.description:
Controls the drawer from a separate object, and not from the `open` prop. Thus a trigger can
be at any position in the tree. Read `createDrawerHandle`.

props.name: triggerRef
props.description: The reference to the trigger element. Set it in your own code, or let Drawer.Trigger set it.

props.name: children
props.description: The children snippet. It receives the state functions.

props.description: The name on the button.

props.name: element
props.description: A bindable reference to the button element.

props.name: payload

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the panel.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
The element that gets the focus when the drawer opens. The default is the first element in the
panel that can take the focus.

props.name: touchAction
props.description:
The `touch-action` value of the panel.

For a left drawer or a right drawer, the default is `pan-y`. The children still scroll on the
vertical axis, and the horizontal axis belongs to the drag.

For a top drawer or a bottom drawer, there is no default. A reservation of the vertical axis
would break each region in the panel that scrolls. `touch-action` applies down the chain of
the parents, and a child cannot cancel it.

dataAttributes.name: data-drawer-bleed
dataAttributes.description: Identifies the strip outside the anchored edge. It covers the page while the panel goes past the open position.
